nodes.label: Scenario-first methodology
nodes.rationale: AI agents build UI without a model of user behavior, so screens accrete feature-by-feature and error/empty/cross-feature states are invented ad hoc or skipped. Fix: a versioned scenario base becomes the source of truth, written and validated before UI is built and used as the audit checklist.

nodes.label: SCN-NNN id and status lifecycle rules
nodes.rationale: IDs are never reused and retired scenarios keep their entry rather than being deleted, so history stays addressable; status runs draft -> validated (human approved) -> implemented (coverage confirmed by audit) -> retired.

nodes.label: Audit verdicts PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL/BLOCKED
nodes.rationale: BLOCKED exists so an auditor with no evidence says why instead of guessing; a guess dressed as a verdict is worse than a declared gap.

nodes.label: ux-scenarios skill (v0.1 design)
nodes.rationale: Four auto-detected workflows (Init greenfield, Init existing code, Update, Validate); new user-facing behavior with no scenario is treated as a blocker, not a warning.

nodes.label: ux-audit skill batch loop (v0.1 design)
nodes.rationale: Scenarios are grouped into batches of ~5-8 by feature and may be dispatched to parallel subagents; each verdict carries file:line evidence, and handoff to a planning workflow is offered rather than auto-run.

nodes.label: test/validate.py repo validator
nodes.rationale: Stdlib-only and non-zero on failure; enforces manifest/CHANGELOG version sync, front-matter presence, template existence and link resolution so drift cannot merge.

nodes.label: Virality and referral cluster (REQ-01)
nodes.rationale: Virality is classified as a mechanism, not a stage or domain; referral is its separately designed special case. Referred users retain better than organic and convert better on freemium, which supplies the why for BP-147.

nodes.label: BP-147 growth loop named before freemium
nodes.rationale: Closes a dangling reference: BP-067 required a growth loop as a precondition for freemium but described it nowhere; the entry forces a concrete loop (viral, content or network) into the foundation next to the model.
nodes.norm_label: bp-147 growth loop named before freemium

nodes.label: BP-148 virality through the product artifact
nodes.rationale: Sharing the output is the lowest-friction mechanism: it requires no new user behavior, only the decision to carry attribution on an artifact that already leaves for third parties.
nodes.norm_label: bp-148 virality through the product artifact

nodes.label: BP-149 plan K near 0.2 and design cycle time
nodes.rationale: The external skill's 0.3-0.7 target sold a strong result as the norm; average B2B SaaS K is about 0.2 and 0.1-0.3 is typical. A fast loop with moderate K beats a slow loop with high K, so cycle time (consumer 7-14 days, B2B 8-12 weeks) is designed, and attribution windows follow from it rather than being arbitrary.

nodes.label: channels.md — one record per surface
nodes.rationale: Platform physics and brand choice are kept as separate fields on purpose: 'a link in the body suppresses reach' and 'we do not post links' are different claims, and merging them makes an algorithm constraint indistinguishable from a decision six months later.

nodes.label: strings.md — interface string decision registry
nodes.rationale: A decision registry, not a message catalog: it records which strings were reconciled with the pack, which scenario each serves and where it lives. Without it, 'one action, two names' is only findable by reading the whole interface. Populated by an inventory sweep, not by hand.

nodes.label: locales/<code>.md — per-locale delta
nodes.rationale: The primary locale is the source of meaning, not of form, so a word-for-word CTA translation is a finding even when grammatical; a locale may lag but must declare it, and parity is reported as a percentage instead of letting an incomplete locale look finished.

nodes.label: Voice pack library — six archetypes
nodes.rationale: operator-brief, calm-expert, peer-builder, editorial-premium, plain-service, playful-consumer; each conforms to a pack contract so a seventh can be authored rather than improvised. Selection proposes one pack with reasoning plus one alternative and says why the runner-up loses.

nodes.label: Pack Failure mode field
nodes.rationale: Every voice has a degenerate form (operator-brief becomes military parody, playful-consumer becomes cringe, calm-expert becomes corporate mush, editorial-premium becomes beautiful emptiness). A pack that names its own overshoot makes it checkable in the audit instead of a matter of opinion; the library is harmful without it.

nodes.label: brand_lint.py
nodes.rationale: Stdlib-only like ux_lint.py and ux_doctor.py; the linter checks only what a machine can prove and everything evaluative goes to the audit. --fix applies only changes that cannot be wrong; exit 0 clean, 1 warnings, 2 errors.

nodes.label: Sources: scan-surface declaration
nodes.rationale: The linter cannot guess where a project keeps its text, so a missing Sources: block is an error (B006): it refuses to report a clean run over a surface it never read. Checks whose source is absent are counted as skipped, never silently passed.

nodes.label: SEO/AEO safety versus optimization split
nodes.rationale: Safety (stuffing, filler, clickbait mismatch, blocked crawlers, unearned superlatives, missing byline) is always on and machine-enforced; optimization (answer front-loading, evidence density, tables, schema, per-engine differences) is on request inside copywriting.

nodes.label: Absolute prohibition on fabricated facts
nodes.rationale: A hard fail, not a score reduction. The Princeton GEO work (KDD 2024) showed a lift from fabrication against GPT-3.5 in 2023, but it is now trained on as an adversarial signal, creates FTC §5 exposure, and the lift evaporates under competition (C-SEO Bench, NeurIPS 2025); real evidence in the same structural pattern captures 80-90% of the effect with none of the risk.

nodes.label: Humanization guards
nodes.rationale: Borrowed from the humanizer methodology, the only surveyed skill treating de-AI-ing as measurable engineering: S1/S2/S3 severity, an A-D grade on the result rather than the input, a 50% change-rate guard, a mandatory semantic-preservation self-check, and a density threshold above which patching is futile.

nodes.label: ux-audit scope copy
nodes.rationale: A new single-pass scope rather than a new skill: it judges what the linter cannot prove — tone drift, the 'could this sit on any other SaaS page' test, so-what failures, unproven claims, narrative coherence, pack failure-mode detection, register mismatch — with file:line evidence and the existing verdict vocabulary.

nodes.rationale: The pack derives from foundation.md; the foundation never changes because a tone was appealing. With no foundation, brand-voice runs degraded, stamps Derived-from: inferred and recommends building the WHY layer first instead of blocking.

nodes.label: Registry adoption cost on legacy projects
nodes.rationale: An inventory sweep on a large product yields hundreds of B022 findings, so B022 is a warning rather than an error: only strings the team has agreed become blocking, and the hard rule is installed by the user's action rather than silently.

nodes.rationale: Order matters: foundation first, then existing copy, then one proposed pack with a named runner-up, then seeding with the Sources: block filled first because nothing can be checked until the linter knows where the text is. Never invent a fact to fill a table.

nodes.label: /brand-lint command
nodes.rationale: A clean linter means checkable, not good — the command is required to say so and offer the audit; with no docs/brand/ it routes to /brand-init rather than linting an absence.

nodes.label: /brand-update command
nodes.rationale: A rename must propagate to terminology.md, strings.md and every locale in the same change — a rename landing in one file and not the others is how two spellings start. A positioning change may deserve a different pack rather than a patched one.

nodes.label: /brand entry point
nodes.rationale: Inspect -> silent repair -> status -> menu with exactly one recommended action; the user is never asked to choose between skills or files, because that vocabulary is internal.

nodes.label: Brand routing table (user words to action)
nodes.norm_label: brand routing table (user words to action)

nodes.label: /copy command
nodes.rationale: First action is reading the pack; no pack means stop and route to /brand-init rather than improvise a voice. Copy is delivered before the reasoning, with two or three headline/CTA options and what each trades away.

nodes.label: /ux-audit command
nodes.rationale: Depth deep runs all five passes (scenarios, flow conformance, heuristics PRN, practices per the selection protocol, chain coverage); single-pass scopes run just that pass.

nodes.label: Contract drift versus internal consistency
nodes.rationale: The linter checks a chain against itself and cannot see that the whole base is written to a contract three versions old, because from the inside such a chain is perfectly consistent. The doctor finds drift between project and contract: mixed versions, unmarked/behind artifacts, files the contract owns under another name, audits with no base. --fix only renames and moves; contract upgrades are content decisions.

nodes.label: /ux-flows command
nodes.rationale: Workflow picked from state and arguments: stories without flows -> Design, existing product without flows.md -> Reverse, improve/fix/redesign -> Improve (heuristic evaluation PRN-01..16 into traced before/after proposals), otherwise Update. After flow changes, every new node and edge needs scenario coverage in the same session.

nodes.label: Settle the style pack before drawing
nodes.rationale: Frames and built screens use one recorded pack's tokens instead of a per-screen palette; inventing a palette, type pairing or motion per screen is visual drift. The sheleg-design companion is recommended, not forced.
nodes.norm_label: settle the style pack before drawing

nodes.label: /ux-foundation command
nodes.rationale: After any change, the cascade check lists scenarios tracing to changed IDs and hands them to ux-scenarios in the same session.

nodes.label: /ux-init command
nodes.rationale: Initializes WHY -> HOW -> WHAT in order and refuses to reinitialize a chain that already has entries; if only some layers exist it initializes the missing ones and leaves the rest untouched.

nodes.label: /ux-lint command
nodes.rationale: Errors are drift or broken structure that must not merge; warnings are gaps to close. Recommended for CI or pre-commit so drift cannot merge silently.

nodes.label: /ux-rule command
nodes.rationale: Idempotent: appends the rule block only when the heading is absent, replaces it when present but divergent, never overwrites seeded user content, and refreshes lint.py because it is code rather than user content.

nodes.label: Installed hard-rule block (UX scenarios + brand voice)
nodes.rationale: Do not write interface code until the foundation -> flows -> screens -> scenarios chain is designed and approved (and mocked in Figma when enabled); building UI before that is the exact mistake super-ux exists to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: installed hard-rule block (ux scenarios + brand voice)

nodes.label: /ux-update command
nodes.rationale: A new feature idea is validated against the chain first — an idea serving no job is challenged, not silently accepted; a change already made runs the Update workflow against the git diff and cascades to flows, screens and Figma links in the same change.

nodes.label: /ux entry point
nodes.rationale: Idempotent single entry: one plain question, routing by the user's own words, silent repair of missing rule/skeleton, a status table across every layer, then only the applicable actions with exactly one marked recommended.

nodes.label: UX routing table (user words to action)
nodes.norm_label: ux routing table (user words to action)

nodes.label: UX inspect state pass
nodes.rationale: Runs both lint.py and doctor.py: a mixed or stale contract is reported before offering any other action, because designing on top of a base three versions behind is how the versions got mixed in the first place.

nodes.label: Plan fixes handoff to task-pipeline
nodes.rationale: Produces docs/ux/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<scope>.md with a per-screen target interface and a traced CREATE/MODIFY/DELETE table prioritized by Frequency x Severity x Solvability, then recommends — never forces — autonomous implementation via task-pipeline.

nodes.label: brand-voice skill
nodes.rationale: Owns docs/brand/ and never deviates from the contract's file, field and status names because the linter and the audit key off them. Invoked with no task it reports status and proposes exactly one next action.

nodes.label: brand-voice workflows: Init, Calibrate, Update, Validate
nodes.norm_label: brand-voice workflows: init, calibrate, update, validate

nodes.label: Voice derives from what the user loses on failure
nodes.rationale: The deciding input from the foundation is the stakes: a voice that charms when the stakes are a playlist is intolerable when the stakes are payroll.
nodes.norm_label: voice derives from what the user loses on failure

nodes.label: Degraded mode (Derived-from: inferred)
nodes.rationale: With no foundation the skill stamps the provenance as inferred, says plainly that the WHY layer should be built, and continues rather than blocking.

nodes.label: Inventory sweep into strings.md
nodes.rationale: Routes, screens, buttons, states, errors and empty states each get a row with file:line and the scenario served; parallel Explore subagents are dispatched one area each for a large codebase.

nodes.label: copywriting skill
nodes.rationale: Reads the pack first every time; guessing a voice and being wrong costs more than the pause, and copy invented surface by surface is exactly the drift this layer exists to remove. It never writes to docs/brand/.

nodes.label: Seven editing sweeps
nodes.rationale: Clarity, voice and tone, so-what, prove-it, specificity, emotion, zero risk — run in order with a loop back after each, but delivered prioritized by impact rather than reading order.

nodes.label: Adapt mode
nodes.rationale: What survives adaptation is the claim and the proof; length, structure, CTA policy and register change. A thread is not a page with line breaks, and each version must state what it drops.

nodes.label: Humanize mode
nodes.rationale: Text that already reads naturally is left alone; editing what is fine to prove the pass ran is this mode's failure.

nodes.label: copywriting non-negotiables
nodes.rationale: No fabricated facts under any framing; no humor on error, destructive confirm, billing or paywall surfaces in any pack; one action keeps one name (a second name is a defect, not a synonym); never quote a number absent from facts.md.

nodes.label: Naturalness grade A-D on the result
nodes.rationale: Graded after the rewrite rather than on the input, so the pass is measured by what it produced.
nodes.norm_label: naturalness grade a-d on the result

nodes.label: Machine-drafting markers catalog
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary, hedging chains, uniform 18-22 word sentences, identical paragraph shape, the rule-of-three habit, em-dash reflex, false balance, summary conclusions, symmetrical headings, over-signposting. Banned words are replaced with the thing they stood in for, never merely deleted; the fix for uniform length is rhythm, not vocabulary.

nodes.label: Vagueness where a fact belongs (S1)
nodes.rationale: 'Many companies', 'studies show', 'significantly improved' each mark a place where a specific claim was avoided because a specific claim can be checked. Replace with the real figure or say plainly there is none — honest absence beats confident vagueness, and this is the B030 rule from the other side.

nodes.label: Density threshold (~10 markers per 500 words)
nodes.rationale: Polishing a piece that is mostly patterns yields the same patterns with better words; saying so and rewriting from the argument is part of the job, not a failure of it.

nodes.label: Change-rate guard (over 50% do not ship)
nodes.rationale: Above half changed it is no longer an edit; it may be the right rewrite, but that is a decision with an owner, and quietly replacing someone's text while calling it a polish is how meaning gets lost unnoticed.

nodes.label: Semantic-preservation checklist
nodes.rationale: Numbers, dates, currency and proper nouns exact; causal direction unchanged; no negation inverted; quotations untouched; core claim and conclusion unchanged; register not drifted upward; every claim still traceable to facts.md. A failure means fix and re-check, not note and proceed.

nodes.label: What 'human' is not
nodes.rationale: Not typos, slang or deliberate roughness. The target is a person who writes well — with a position, specific knowledge and a reason to have written this — and friction is added only where a real writer would have it.

nodes.label: Channel Playbooks — the physics of each surface
nodes.norm_label: channel playbooks — the physics of each surface

nodes.label: Marketing copy — pages, posts and long form
nodes.norm_label: marketing copy — pages, posts and long form

nodes.label: Search and answer engines — safety first
nodes.norm_label: search and answer engines — safety first

nodes.label: Store listings — App Store and Google Play
nodes.norm_label: store listings — app store and google play

nodes.label: Surface registers — one voice, many surfaces
nodes.norm_label: surface registers — one voice, many surfaces

nodes.label: UI copy — the strings inside the product
nodes.norm_label: ui copy — the strings inside the product

nodes.label: UX Design Principles — How the Agent Thinks
nodes.norm_label: ux design principles — how the agent thinks

nodes.label: BP tag taxonomy (stage/mechanism/domain/channel/craft/verbal/components)
nodes.rationale: Tags are the retrieval axis: filter by tag, open only matching entries, because reading the whole 1500-line catalog to find three practices is a real cost.

nodes.label: BP-001 Adapt competitor tactics, don't copy them
nodes.rationale: The one practice that ALWAYS applies; it is the anti-cargo-cult anchor — a practice is adopted only when it serves a traced job/story of THIS product.
nodes.norm_label: bp-001 adapt competitor tactics, don't copy them

nodes.label: Visual craft cluster BP-079..090 (typography, color, layout)
nodes.rationale: These are floors, never an identity — the concrete palette/type/motion come from a locked style pack.
nodes.norm_label: visual craft cluster bp-079..090 (typography, color, layout)

nodes.label: Web funnels cluster BP-116..123 (landing, pricing, checkout, billing, cancel)
nodes.norm_label: web funnels cluster bp-116..123 (landing, pricing, checkout, billing, cancel)

nodes.label: Motion cluster BP-130..132 (token scale, reduced motion, scroll-driven floors)
nodes.norm_label: motion cluster bp-130..132 (token scale, reduced motion, scroll-driven floors)

nodes.label: Accessibility-as-it-fails cluster BP-136..138
nodes.rationale: Overlays are not remediation and scanners are not coverage; accessibility is decided in the chain, not retrofitted after build.

nodes.label: Trend adoption & visual debt cluster BP-145..146
nodes.rationale: A trend with no named mechanism, no owner and no review date is debt on arrival; styles with known debt ship only with the compensation named.
nodes.norm_label: trend adoption & visual debt cluster bp-145..146

nodes.label: Growth loops, virality & referral cluster BP-147..151
nodes.norm_label: growth loops, virality & referral cluster bp-147..151

nodes.label: Empty states, authentication & form recovery cluster BP-152..156
nodes.norm_label: empty states, authentication & form recovery cluster bp-152..156

nodes.label: Motion craft cluster BP-157..164 (duration, easing, origin, interruptibility)
nodes.rationale: The decisions BP-130's token scale does not make: whether it animates at all, how long, which easing, where it enters from, and whether it can be interrupted.
nodes.norm_label: motion craft cluster bp-157..164 (duration, easing, origin, interruptibility)

nodes.label: Perceived quality cluster BP-165..168 (icons, emoji, pressed states, scrim)
nodes.rationale: Why a correct interface still looks unfinished — the defects live below the level anyone writes a ticket about.
nodes.norm_label: perceived quality cluster bp-165..168 (icons, emoji, pressed states, scrim)

nodes.label: Generated-default tells cluster BP-169..172
nodes.rationale: The signature of a decision nobody made: fake screenshots, decorative placeholders, the three-equal-cards row, defaults that betray an unmade choice.

nodes.label: Interface state, platform surfaces & locale cluster BP-173..179
nodes.norm_label: interface state, platform surfaces & locale cluster bp-173..179

nodes.label: Tag → BP-id index (82 tags, 206 practices)
nodes.rationale: Makes finding practices cheap without deciding what is mandatory — that stays with the selection protocol.

nodes.label: bp_index.py generator + drift validator
nodes.rationale: The index is generated, never hand-edited; the validator fails when index and catalog disagree, and --stale reports Checked-date ages so they are not baked into a generated file.

nodes.label: Motivation principles PRN-17..PRN-21 and their coercive twins
nodes.rationale: Every motivation lever has a coercive twin aimed at the product's interest; a mechanism that only works while the user misunderstands the situation is a dark pattern wearing a principle's name, so an applied verdict must name which side it is on.
nodes.norm_label: motivation principles prn-17..prn-21 and their coercive twins

nodes.label: Voice principles PRN-22..PRN-24
nodes.rationale: They sit beside the interaction principles rather than under them: a product can satisfy every heuristic and still read like three different companies.

nodes.label: PRN-14 Jakob's law — deviate only when the job demands it
nodes.rationale: Users spend most of their time in OTHER apps, so the platform's standard component ships with accessibility, states and motion behavior you would otherwise rebuild wrong.
nodes.norm_label: prn-14 jakob's law — deviate only when the job demands it

nodes.label: PRN-22 One voice, many registers
nodes.rationale: Violated when a surface quietly breaks an invariant because it 'needs a different tone' — improvisation dressed as adaptation.

nodes.label: PRN-24 Never joke about the user's loss
nodes.norm_label: prn-24 never joke about the user's loss

nodes.label: The 8-step design pipeline (RESEARCH → VERIFY)
nodes.rationale: UI code comes only at step 7: never design a screen before its flow exists, never draw a flow for a story that traces to no job.

nodes.label: Forward mode vs backwards mode (inferred tagging)
nodes.rationale: For an existing product the same artifacts are filled in reverse from code and tagged `inferred` until a human confirms; the gaps between 'is' and 'should' become the improvement backlog.
nodes.norm_label: forward mode vs backwards mode (inferred tagging)

nodes.label: Task analysis method (decompose, cut, mark first value)
nodes.rationale: Aha is engineered, not hoped for — mark the step where the user first receives real value and reach it as early as possible.
nodes.norm_label: task analysis method (decompose, cut, mark first value)

nodes.label: Flow design rules (branches, error edges, entry points, ≤5 steps)
nodes.rationale: Dead ends are defects by definition; a flow entered mid-way must still work, so every entry point is enumerated.
nodes.norm_label: flow design rules (branches, error edges, entry points, ≤5 steps)

nodes.label: Screen & interaction rules (one primary action, states, a11y in text)
nodes.rationale: Accessibility and motion are decided here in text, not after the UI exists; retrofitting is the expensive way to reach the same place.
nodes.norm_label: screen & interaction rules (one primary action, states, a11y in text)

nodes.label: Design anti-patterns (stop signals)
nodes.rationale: Dark patterns at the paywall create churn and refunds, not LTV — the conversion moment is not exempt from the honesty rules.

nodes.label: Heuristic evaluation procedure for improving existing UX
nodes.rationale: You cannot judge UX without knowing the intended jobs, so a backwards-mode chain is a prerequisite; 'make it prettier' is not a proposal.
nodes.norm_label: heuristic evaluation procedure for improving existing ux

nodes.label: Step 2 — Mandatory consideration sets from the profile
nodes.rationale: 'Mandatory consideration' means an explicit verdict, never automatic adoption — nothing relevant silently skipped, nothing irrelevant cargo-culted.
nodes.norm_label: step 2 — mandatory consideration sets from the profile

nodes.label: Step 4 — Compliance table (applied / adapted / rejected / deferred)
nodes.rationale: A verdict without a trace is fiction; user-owned rejections (taste, brand, strategy) are recorded and never re-litigated on every pass.
nodes.norm_label: step 4 — compliance table (applied / adapted / rejected / deferred)

nodes.label: Anti-cargo-cult rule + conflict resolution
nodes.rationale: When two practices conflict the foundation's Monetization section decides, and the conflict plus the decision go into the compliance table.

nodes.label: Style pack vs practices — identity wins on look, floors win on safety
nodes.rationale: The pack owns palette, type pairing, motion tokens and bans; the practices own contrast, tap targets, line length and spacing rhythm — record any conflict and its resolution like any other verdict.
nodes.norm_label: style pack vs practices — identity wins on look, floors win on safety

nodes.label: ux-contract v4 (field names, ID schemes, statuses, verdicts)
nodes.rationale: Tooling and audits key off the field names, so deviation is forbidden; the design reasoning behind the formats lives in the principles doc instead.
nodes.norm_label: ux-contract v4 (field names, id schemes, statuses, verdicts)

nodes.label: flows.md — the HOW layer (task analysis + mermaid flows)
nodes.norm_label: flows.md — the how layer (task analysis + mermaid flows)

nodes.label: screens.md — the UI map (screens, states, frames, coverage)
nodes.rationale: A screen used by several flows is described in exactly one place; flows list only which of its states they traverse, so specs are never duplicated.
nodes.norm_label: screens.md — the ui map (screens, states, frames, coverage)

nodes.label: Same-change update rule (all layers)
nodes.rationale: A screen whose code diverges from its screens.md record, or a stale/broken Figma link, is a `drifted` finding — not an acceptable state.

nodes.label: Traceability rules (orphans in either direction are findings)
nodes.norm_label: traceability rules (orphans in either direction are findings)

nodes.label: Telemetry field (object_action snake_case, verb last)
nodes.rationale: The bridge the chain was missing: telemetry practices assume events exist, but nothing tied a named event to the behavior it measures, so renaming a step silently made the dashboard measure something else.

nodes.label: Kill criteria on a user story (optional)
nodes.rationale: `dropped` existed as a status with nothing defining when it applies, so it was only ever reached by someone losing interest — the slowest possible way to learn.
nodes.norm_label: kill criteria on a user story (optional)

nodes.label: Scenario `Strings:` field — keys, not text
nodes.rationale: Lets a copy audit go from a scenario to the exact strings that serve it, and lets the brand linter tell a string that serves a real scenario from one nobody claims.

nodes.label: The verdict fork — REFINE / REDESIGN / NEW
nodes.rationale: Findings alone read as a to-do list, so a surface that should be rebuilt gets patched indefinitely, one true finding at a time, and every round looks like progress.
nodes.norm_label: the verdict fork — refine / redesign / new

nodes.label: Scope and limits section (not optional)
nodes.rationale: An audit reads a finite slice of the code, so silence about the rest reads as coverage — absence of a scenario from the report never means PASS.

nodes.label: UX plan format (target interface + CREATE/MODIFY/DELETE)
nodes.rationale: Written so an autonomous agent can execute it without the conversation; an untraced change does not enter the plan.

nodes.label: brand-contract v1 — the docs/brand/ contract
nodes.rationale: docs/ux/ answers what the product does, docs/brand/ answers how it speaks; they are separate roots because the brand pack also governs surfaces that are not UX at all. The `Contract: brand-contract v1` marker on line 1 of every file lets ux_doctor tell a base written to an old contract from a current one — a base three versions behind is internally consistent, which is precisely why a linter cannot see it.

nodes.label: voice.md — pack, five axes, narrative, invariants, locales
nodes.rationale: Derived from foundation.md one way only — a persona does not change because a tone was appealing; the trace is recorded in `Derived-from:`.
nodes.norm_label: voice.md — pack, five axes, narrative, invariants, locales

nodes.label: The five fixed axes (Confidence, Register, Distance, Humor, Density)
nodes.rationale: A project may sharpen the wording but may not add or remove an axis, because channels.md expresses register as deltas against exactly these five.
nodes.norm_label: the five fixed axes (confidence, register, distance, humor, density)

nodes.label: terminology.md — our words, banned words, entity and tier names
nodes.norm_label: terminology.md — our words, banned words, entity and tier names

nodes.label: facts.md — the only source of any figure in public copy
nodes.rationale: A number in a public surface with no row here blocks (B030); a missing fact is reported, never invented to close a gap.
nodes.norm_label: facts.md — the only source of any figure in public copy

nodes.label: channels.md — one record per surface (register, limits, bans)
nodes.rationale: A project may omit a surface it does not have but may not rename one: the linter and the audit both address surfaces by these names.
nodes.norm_label: channels.md — one record per surface (register, limits, bans)

nodes.label: strings.md — interface string decision registry
nodes.rationale: A decision registry, not a message catalog: it is what makes B020 (one action, two names) checkable at all — without it that defect is only findable by reading the whole interface.

nodes.label: README.md `Sources:` block — the paths that get scanned
nodes.rationale: The one thing the linter cannot infer; a missing block blocks (B006) because the linter refuses to report a clean run over a surface it never read.
nodes.norm_label: readme.md `sources:` block — the paths that get scanned

nodes.label: B061 — humor banned on error, destructive confirm, billing, paywall
nodes.rationale: The user is losing data, access or money at that moment; a joke reads as mockery. Enforced in every pack including playful-consumer, and not left to taste.
nodes.norm_label: b061 — humor banned on error, destructive confirm, billing, paywall

nodes.label: The register model (voice axes ± per-surface deltas)
nodes.rationale: A product has one voice and roughly two dozen surfaces; solving that with two dozen voices is how a product ends up reading like three different companies. Three steps in either direction is the practical range before the voice stops being recognisable.
nodes.norm_label: the register model (voice axes ± per-surface deltas)

nodes.label: Rule 1 — a register moves the axes, never the invariants
nodes.rationale: Keeps per-surface freedom from becoming per-surface improvisation: either the invariant was wrong and voice.md changes for the whole product, or the surface is wrong for this product and is not used. Both are decisions with an owner.
nodes.norm_label: rule 1 — a register moves the axes, never the invariants

nodes.label: Rule 2 — platform physics and brand choice are different fields
nodes.rationale: Written on one line they become indistinguishable within a quarter, and then nobody can tell which one is safe to revisit when the platform changes its ranking. The linter enforces the physics half because it is mechanical; the brand half is judged by the copy audit because it is a decision.
nodes.norm_label: rule 2 — platform physics and brand choice are different fields

nodes.label: Rule 3 — humor forbidden where the user is losing something
nodes.rationale: Not a register delta, because a delta is negotiable and this is not.
nodes.norm_label: rule 3 — humor forbidden where the user is losing something

nodes.label: Product surface registers (primary action → docs and help)
nodes.norm_label: product surface registers (primary action → docs and help)

nodes.label: Marketing surface registers (landing hero → lifecycle email)
nodes.norm_label: marketing surface registers (landing hero → lifecycle email)

nodes.label: The pack contract (nine fields every pack carries)
nodes.rationale: A pack is a starting position, not the answer: it is calibrated until voice.md is the truth and the pack name survives only as provenance. The deciding input when picking one is what the user loses when the product fails.
nodes.norm_label: the pack contract (nine fields every pack carries)

nodes.label: `Failure mode` — the mandatory declared overshoot
nodes.rationale: Every voice's overshoot sounds MORE like the pack, not less, which is why nobody catches it from inside; naming it up front turns 'this feels like too much' into a checkable finding. A pack without it is an instruction to overshoot with no brake.

nodes.label: Pack: operator-brief
nodes.rationale: Assumes competence and reads as contempt when that assumption is wrong; degenerates into military-jargon parody.

nodes.label: Pack: calm-expert
nodes.rationale: Trusted and rarely shared; degenerates into corporate mush where every sentence acquires a qualifier.

nodes.label: Pack: peer-builder
nodes.rationale: Degenerates into insider shorthand, or honesty performed rather than practised — limits listed for credit while the real one stays buried.

nodes.label: Pack: editorial-premium
nodes.rationale: Degenerates into beautiful emptiness: the rhythm survives, the content leaves.

nodes.label: Pack: plain-service
nodes.rationale: Cannot make anyone want something; it makes things possible. Degenerates into flatness that reads as indifference.

nodes.label: Pack: playful-consumer
nodes.rationale: Degenerates into cringe — copy that is funny on the first read and obstructive on the fortieth, because microcopy is read hundreds of times and a joke has a half-life.

nodes.label: Platform physics per marketing surface
nodes.rationale: Kept apart from register on purpose: merged, the two become indistinguishable within a quarter and nobody can tell which half is safe to revisit when a platform changes.

nodes.label: Physics decays — every ranking behaviour carries a checked date
nodes.rationale: A rule older than its review date is a hypothesis, not a constraint; a rule with no date cannot be audited, only believed.
nodes.norm_label: physics decays — every ranking behaviour carries a checked date

nodes.label: Four inputs before writing (action, reader, their words, proof)
nodes.rationale: Copy that names the problem in the reader's words outperforms copy that names it in the company's, and the gap is not close.
nodes.norm_label: four inputs before writing (action, reader, their words, proof)

nodes.label: Page structure (headline → final CTA) and page types
nodes.rationale: One idea per section — a section that advances two arguments advances neither.
nodes.norm_label: page structure (headline → final cta) and page types

nodes.label: The seven sweeps (clarity → zero risk)
nodes.rationale: Run in order, re-checking earlier sweeps after each one because a fix in one dimension routinely breaks an earlier one. Emotion that replaces the argument is manipulation and out of bounds.

nodes.label: The grounding model (prerequisite vs introduced)
nodes.rationale: A passage that reaches for an ungrounded concept loses the reader, and the loss is silent; the unit is the concept, not the word, so a paragraph can lean on an idea the reader lacks with no jargon in sight.

nodes.label: Comparison-page honesty rule (concede something real)
nodes.rationale: A comparison with no line naming what the competitor does better is read as an advertisement and discounted entirely — the concession is what makes the rest credible.

nodes.label: The four laws of UI copy
nodes.rationale: Interface copy is read hundreds of times by the same person, so a line that is charming on the first read is an obstruction on the fortieth — that is why UI craft disagrees with marketing craft. Two names for one action is the most common defect in a product built screen by screen, because each screen was individually correct.
nodes.norm_label: the four laws of ui copy

nodes.label: Errors carry three facts (what happened, what survived, one next step)
nodes.rationale: The middle fact is the one products skip and users need most — 'your draft was saved' turns a failure into an interruption. A code with no sentence beside it is a support ticket the user has to write.
nodes.norm_label: errors carry three facts (what happened, what survived, one next step)

nodes.label: Empty states teach; three kinds need different copy
nodes.rationale: Nothing yet (teach), nothing matched (offer to widen the filter), nothing left (confirm completion, do not imply failure).
nodes.norm_label: empty states teach; three kinds need different copy

nodes.label: Accessibility is copy work too (accessible name = visible label)
nodes.rationale: A button reading Delete with an accessible name of Remove item is two names for one action — B020 with a screen reader as the witness.
nodes.norm_label: accessibility is copy work too (accessible name = visible label)

nodes.label: What travels and what does not (invariant vs reconsidered per locale)
nodes.rationale: Some of a voice is invariant and some has to be decided again per language; the difference has to be written down or every locale quietly becomes its own brand. Address form changes perception more than any word choice.
nodes.norm_label: what travels and what does not (invariant vs reconsidered per locale)

nodes.label: Length coefficient (multiplies every field limit per locale)
nodes.rationale: The tightest surfaces break first; a 30-character App Store title at 1.3 leaves 23 characters of meaning — a design constraint on the English original, not a translation problem discovered later.
nodes.norm_label: length coefficient (multiplies every field limit per locale)

nodes.label: Translate the job the string does, not the words (B072)
nodes.rationale: The primary locale is the source of meaning, not of form: a word-for-word CTA is grammatically perfect and nobody clicks it. The shorter the string, the more its impact depends on idiom.
nodes.norm_label: translate the job the string does, not the words (b072)

nodes.label: Parity declared rather than hidden (B071)
nodes.rationale: A partial locale that declares itself is a known state; one that does not is a surprise waiting for a user who does not speak the fallback.

nodes.label: Keywords are researched per market, never translated
nodes.rationale: The translation of a high-volume English keyword is routinely a term with no volume; if the market's questions differ, the headings differ too.
nodes.norm_label: keywords are researched per market, never translated

nodes.label: The absolute rule — no fabricated facts, quotes, statistics or experts
nodes.rationale: The GEO24 visibility lift from fabricated citations is a closed window: fabrication is now trained against as an adversarial signal, it creates FTC §5 exposure, and the lift evaporates under competition (C-SEO Bench, NeurIPS 2025). Real evidence in the same structural patterns captures most of the effect with none of the risk.
nodes.norm_label: the absolute rule — no fabricated facts, quotes, statistics or experts

nodes.label: The safety veto list (blocked crawlers, clickbait mismatch, no byline)
nodes.rationale: Any veto caps the value of everything else on the page; a page that is optimized and unsafe is a liability that also stops working, so safety precedes optimization by order, not preference.
nodes.norm_label: the safety veto list (blocked crawlers, clickbait mismatch, no byline)

nodes.label: Optimization — structure that makes content extractable
nodes.rationale: Extraction is structural: position weighting decays sharply, and a sentence that needs the previous paragraph to make sense cannot be quoted, and therefore is not.
nodes.norm_label: optimization — structure that makes content extractable

nodes.label: Technical floor (robots.txt, no-JS rendering, semantic HTML, schema)
nodes.rationale: Declaring AI search as a target while blocking GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot is the contradiction B050 exists to catch.
nodes.norm_label: technical floor (robots.txt, no-js rendering, semantic html, schema)

nodes.label: Store field limits and the two structural differences
nodes.rationale: App Store has a hidden keyword field while Google Play indexes the description, so the two descriptions are written for different readers; promotional text is the only field changeable between releases, which makes it the place for anything time-bound.
nodes.norm_label: store field limits and the two structural differences

nodes.label: The iOS keyword field (B041 — four rules)
nodes.rationale: 100 characters and most listings waste a third: no space after commas, no plurals, nothing already in the title or subtitle, no competitor brand names (grounds for rejection, not a style preference).
nodes.norm_label: the ios keyword field (b041 — four rules)

nodes.label: Screenshot captions name the outcome, not the UI
nodes.rationale: The caption is read before the screenshot is understood, so it carries the value; the first screenshot does the work of a headline.
nodes.norm_label: screenshot captions name the outcome, not the ui

nodes.label: Choosing a control by the job (decision matrix)
nodes.rationale: Distilled from Apple HIG, Material Design 3, W3C ARIA APG and the GOV.UK Design System — the rule above all is to reach for the platform's standard component before inventing one.
nodes.norm_label: choosing a control by the job (decision matrix)

nodes.label: Every interactive component ships all its states
nodes.rationale: Default is not a component; missing states are how PRN-01/PRN-09 silently fail, so the audit checks the state set and Figma variants must carry them.
nodes.norm_label: every interactive component ships all its states

nodes.label: Cross-platform stance (component of record, native before ARIA)
nodes.rationale: Pages carrying ARIA measure worse than pages without it, because every role is behavior the author must then implement by hand.
nodes.norm_label: cross-platform stance (component of record, native before aria)

nodes.label: Figma preflight (MCP present, load Figma's own skill, file, library, style pack)
nodes.rationale: The MCP gates its main tools behind guidance skills and skipping them is the most common cause of hard-to-debug failures; a missing MCP never blocks the chain, it degrades to markdown and syncs later.
nodes.norm_label: figma preflight (mcp present, load figma's own skill, file, library, style pack)

nodes.label: Which Figma MCP tool for which job
nodes.rationale: Treat the list as a map, not a contract: if a tool is missing in the user's setup, degrade to what is there and say so — never invent a call.
nodes.norm_label: which figma mcp tool for which job

nodes.label: The Figma design loop inside ux-flows Design
nodes.rationale: The pack supplies the values, the visual-craft practices are the floor those values must clear; the compliance table then records those BPs as applied with the Figma frame as evidence.
nodes.norm_label: the figma design loop inside ux-flows design

nodes.label: Figma sync rule and boundaries (a rendering, never a replacement)
nodes.rationale: Flows, screens and scenarios remain the source of truth; a frame that drifts from its screen record is a finding, and the screens.md registry is the index that makes drift checkable.
nodes.norm_label: figma sync rule and boundaries (a rendering, never a replacement)

nodes.label: Names ARE the index (1:1 Figma ↔ super-ux IDs)
nodes.rationale: Every Figma object is named to match a super-ux ID so lookup is deterministic — no hunting, no guessing; that is the whole navigation model.
nodes.norm_label: names are the index (1:1 figma ↔ super-ux ids)

nodes.label: Frame naming SCR-NN/<Screen>/<state> — the backbone
nodes.rationale: Exactly the states listed in that screen's States table — no more, no fewer: a missing frame for a listed state is drift, a frame with no state row is an orphan.

nodes.label: Page order (Cover, Index, Design system, one page per flow, Scratch)
nodes.norm_label: page order (cover, index, design system, one page per flow, scratch)

nodes.label: Variables as tokens — primitive → semantic → component
nodes.rationale: Components reference semantic tokens, never raw values; auto layout on every container is what makes frames translate to real layout code.
nodes.norm_label: variables as tokens — primitive → semantic → component

nodes.label: What the agent checks (frame parity, orphans, token references)
nodes.rationale: get_metadata is the cheap read that confirms a frame still exists under its expected name without pulling full design context; get_variable_defs makes 'built on the tokens' checkable rather than assumed.
nodes.norm_label: what the agent checks (frame parity, orphans, token references)

nodes.label: The locked style pack (palette, type, texture, motion tokens, bans)
nodes.rationale: super-ux deliberately does not invent a look: a palette, type pairing, texture and motion vocabulary invented per screen drift into a collage — the visual half of the same drift the system exists to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: the locked style pack (palette, type, texture, motion tokens, bans)

nodes.label: Division of labor — super-ux vs sheleg-design
nodes.rationale: On conflict the pack wins on identity and the practices win on floors — a pack may not push contrast below the WCAG floor or tap targets under the platform minimum.
nodes.norm_label: division of labor — super-ux vs sheleg-design

nodes.label: sheleg-design companion (recommended, never forced)
nodes.rationale: One offer with its one-time install, then the user's answer stands; a declined pack is recorded as 'none — platform defaults' and never re-asked. If a project already has a design system, that IS the identity — two identities is worse than any single one.

nodes.label: What the audit checks when a Style pack is recorded
nodes.rationale: A frame carrying raw hexes where the pack has variables is the design-side twin of hard-coded colors in code; the look is the user's call but the BP-146 compensation is not optional.
nodes.norm_label: what the audit checks when a style pack is recorded

nodes.label: The super-ux pipeline (WHY → HOW → UI map → WHAT → evidence → action)
nodes.rationale: Build forward for new work, fill backward tagged `inferred` for an existing product; UI code comes only after the chain is designed and approved.
nodes.norm_label: the super-ux pipeline (why → how → ui map → what → evidence → action)

nodes.label: The four rules that keep agents in sync
nodes.rationale: Chain-first, same-change, no drift, run the linter — wired into CI/pre-commit so drift cannot merge.
nodes.norm_label: the four rules that keep agents in sync

nodes.label: /ux — the single entry point
nodes.rationale: Users never pick skills: /ux asks the task in plain words, routes to the right workflow and reports status.

nodes.label: Companions — sheleg-design and task-pipeline (offers, not dependencies)
nodes.norm_label: companions — sheleg-design and task-pipeline (offers, not dependencies)

nodes.label: docs/brand/ as a separate root beside docs/ux/
nodes.rationale: Separate because the brand also governs surfaces that are not UX — a store listing, an ad, a post. The pack derives from foundation.md and never the reverse; copywriting writes from it and never to it.
nodes.norm_label: docs/brand/ as a separate root beside docs/ux/

nodes.label: Copy scope — the seven judgement passes
nodes.rationale: The twin of brand_lint.py: the linter proves the mechanical half, this judges the half that needs a reader. A clean linter means checkable, not good — saying so is the point of running both. Without a recorded pack there is nothing to judge against except taste.
nodes.norm_label: copy scope — the seven judgement passes

nodes.label: Benchmark scope — measuring against a named competitor
nodes.rationale: Every other scope measures the product against its own chain, which cannot report that the whole flow is two steps longer than everyone else's. A gap against a competitor is an opportunity, not a defect — it becomes a story in the foundation, not a fix in this report.
nodes.norm_label: benchmark scope — measuring against a named competitor

nodes.label: Evidence discipline — file:line or BLOCKED
nodes.rationale: Never a guess, never a courtesy PASS — an audit that flatters the codebase is worthless.

nodes.label: Pass 1 — scenario pass (code vs every scoped scenario)
nodes.norm_label: pass 1 — scenario pass (code vs every scoped scenario)

nodes.label: Pass 4 — practice pass (selection protocol + compliance table)

nodes.norm_label: pass 4 — practice pass (selection protocol + compliance table)

nodes.label: The audit loop (scope → batch → audit → report → update → plan)
nodes.rationale: The report is written batch by batch as results arrive, because a crashed run must leave the completed batches on disk; large scopes dispatch one subagent per batch.
nodes.norm_label: the audit loop (scope → batch → audit → report → update → plan)

nodes.label: Pass semantics — PRN/BP findings are opportunities, not blockers
nodes.rationale: They do not change scenario verdicts unless the violation breaks a scenario; practices are opportunities selected by the protocol, not a style gate.
